pr_title: Don't let the UTF8OutPipeReader be static
pr_comments: /cc @german-one (i can't request a review from you, but you can still sign off if this makes sense :smile:)

Thanks for keeping me updated!

How embarrassing for me. I discussed with @miniksa about a static class instance in `WriteConsoleA` which seems to made me blind for the different preconditions here. However, there is no excuse.

Would you mind to update this line too?
https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/blob/8d52ba0990f89de552b572381adb26b77cee847b/src/types/ut_types/UTF8OutPipeReaderTests.cpp#L124
`UTF8OutPipeReader reader{ outPipe }; // declare an instance of UTF8OutPipeReader`  
Not that this would make any difference here. Just to reconcile it with the productive code.

Hold on a second
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/46659645/61394689-f9876580-a8c3-11e9-870d-770cc6517893.png)
Seems ~~updating~~ running the Unit Test was a real good idea. I already have a rough idea why this fails. It's likely that we can't work with `std::string_view&` any longer in `UTF8OutPipeReader::Read`.
Unless the individual calls to `RunTest` were intended to rely on static state stored in the UTF8OPutPipeReader (partials from one test flowing into the next test), making it non-static was correct.
Yes this was definitely correct. I feel responsible for that. Just give me some minutes figuring out what's going wrong ...
Having `if (!fSuccess)` before `if (dwRead == 0)` makes it fail. Even though I agree that this order is correct...

The reason why I originally checked `if (dwRead == 0)` first was because of that piece of the comment:

> // quit if no data has been read **and no cached data was left over**

Now that we escape if `RadFile` failed, we may still have data in the buffer that has been cached before.
If there's data in the buffer that was cached, but ReadFile failed, that data can't be used. It's still a partial UTF-8 sequence!
Absolutely. So we could just discard it and return the fail.
Okay, this is now a little different. I've cleaned up some of the code and added another _successful_ exit case (reading from a closed pipe is a detectable 0-byte "successful" read.)
I switched away from using `unique_hfile` because that's only supposed to be used when it _owns_ a handle. Holding a reference to a unique_hfile is the same as holding a raw HANDLE!
I like this. Looks a little like my proposal above.

issue_context.body: Whoops, I just realized why this was happening. I opened a new tab and the output from a different shell showed up in it.
